[[File:BunchaJedi-Rep65.jpg|thumb|right|130px|Windu during his mission to The Rig.]] Windu's team successfully breached The Rig's security. The bounties were rescinded, and the originator, [[Kh'aris Fenn]], was later executed by [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]]. ====Mission to the Leisure Satellite==== ''Main article: [[Mission to the leisure satellite]]'' [[File:Mission_to_the_leisure_satellite_2.jpg|left|thumb|220x220px|Windu attacks Ventress on the leisure satellite.]] A [[Squad/Legends|squad]] of battle droids attempted to construct a [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannon]] on a leisure satellite orbiting Coruscant, with which they were to destroy the [[Senate Building/Legends|Senate Building]] on the surface of the planet. Das unsuccessfully bombarded the refinery with gunfire, failing to destory it and fleeing into space in his starship. I know the name.|Palpatine on the name of Darth Sidious to Mace Windu and Yoda|''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''}} In the aftermath of the [[Siege of Cato Neimoidia|battle]] on Cato Neimoidia, the Jedi Order recovered a valuable [[Mechno-chair/Legends|mechno-chair]] which personally belonged to Trade Federation Viceroy Nute Gunray who used the chair to communicate directly to the hidden [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] Darth Sidious. But Windu and Ti disengaged when Coruscant [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|fell under attack]] by Grievous. ====Battle of Coruscant==== {{Main|Battle of Coruscant/Legends}} {{Quote|A very, very wise Jedi once said to me, 'we don't have to win. All we have to do is fight.'|Obi-Wan Kenobi, on Mace Windu|}} [[File:YodaMaceCoruscant.jpg|thumb|left|Windu with Yoda during the battle.]] Towards the end of the Clone Wars General Grievous orchestrated a surprise attack on Coruscant itself. During the battle Windu piloted his personal ship around the capital and destroyed huge numbers of the Separatist's forces. However, he was eventually forced to abandon his craft and took control of a droid ship; using it to take down several of its fellows. After this, Windu apparently dueled Grievous himself atop a moving train and defeated the notorious cyborg, knocking him from the train. Windu subsequently joined Yoda and aided him to hold the Republic's line against the masses of Separatist battle droids. The two highest ranking members among the Order soon began to question why Grievous had launched such an attack without trying to capture the Jedi Temple or the Senate. It soon became clear that he had orchestrated the attack as a ruse to hide his true objective; the capture of Chancellor Palpatine.{{CW|25}} Grievous successfully captured Palpatine, though before he tried to take the captive Chancellor back to his ship, the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']], he was confronted by Mace Windu. Using Force Crush, Mace Windu devastated Grievous' armor and organs (the lungs in particular). This accounts for the coughing fits the cyborg would face during the end of his life. However, the general survived and escaped with Palpatine; though Kenobi and Skywalker would ultimately rescue him, and kill Count Dooku himself. ====Growing darkness==== {{Quote|I sense a plot to destroy the Jedi. The dark side of the Force surrounds the Chancellor.|Mace Windu, voicing his concern for the future of the Jedi|}} The Clone Wars divided the Republic not only within its territorial sovereignty, but also at its highest level of authority. Near the end of the conflict, the masters of the Jedi High Council became increasingly alarmed at the Supreme Chancellor's rapid transformation into a virtual dictator. As the Senate continued to voluntarily surrender its executive powers to Chancellor Palpatine, Master Windu became suspicious of Palpatine's motives. The war was ending, yet Palpatine was implementing stronger measures of political and social control over the Republic. Even the Senate itself was becoming little more than an advisory board and a rubber stamp for passing Palpatine's draconian laws. Shortly after the Battle of Coruscant, Windu and a group of Senators personally greeted Palpatine after Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi freed him from the clutches of General Grievous and Count Dooku. When Palpatine insisted that the war would still carry on since the Separatists survived the death of Count Dooku, Windu vowed that the Jedi would prioritize the destruction of General Grievous, the last visible symbol of the Separatist cause, thus depriving the Chancellor of his last valid excuse to hold on to his emergency powers. In the days that followed, the Jedi were on the lookout for ways of ''peacefully'' removing Palpatine from office. But relations between the Jedi Council and the Chancellor became so strained to the point where they no longer trusted the Chancellor to keep his word and lay down his emergency powers at the end of the war. The Council was further concerned about the Chancellor when out of the blue, he appointed Anakin Skywalker to sit as his personal representative on the Council, startling members of the Council such as Windu, Yoda and Kenobi. Windu said that Skywalker was on the Council, but he would not become a Master, a decision that made Skywalker begin to question the Council and its motives. Shortly after, the Council discussed the Separatist [[Battle of Kashyyyk/Legends|attack]] on [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], to which Yoda said he would go to aid the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] people. Shortly afterwards, the Council decided that they needed to spy on the Chancellor and find out what he was up to. They tasked Kenobi with giving the task of spying to Skywalker, to which Kenobi tried to rebuke at first but relented. While Windu and Kenobi were in a LAAT gunship escorting Yoda to his ship for his departure, Windu said that it was dangerous pairing Palpatine and Skywalker together. Windu did not trust Skywalker and Kenobi asked if he really was the Chosen One. Sometime after that, Skywalker brought to the Council information that Grievous had hid on [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]] with the [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]]. The Jedi Knight further added that Palpatine wanted Skywalker to personally go to Utapau. Windu scolded this and said that the Council would decide, not the Chancellor. Master Kenobi was voted to [[Battle of Utapau/Legends|deal]] with Grievous due to his experiences with the cyborg. At a later stage, Commander Cody reported that he and Kenobi had commenced their attack on Utapau and that the Jedi Master had engaged Grievous in a [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|duel]]. Windu tasked Skywalker with informing Palpatine of this. He also told Skywalker to look at his reaction so as to see his intentions. Once Skywalker left, Windu stated to Yoda, Ki-Adi-Mundi and Aayla Secura that the Dark Side surrounded Palpatine and that he sensed a sinister plot to eradicate the Jedi. Mundi declared that unless Palpatine stepped down after General Kenobi killed Grievous, then the Jedi would have no other choice but to remove the Chancellor from office by force. Thinking pragmatically, Windu concluded that the Jedi Council would have to seize control of the Senate in order to secure a peaceful transition of power to a new Chancellor. Master Yoda feared where such a line of thought would lead the Jedi Order, but even Yoda himself was weary of the Chancellor's actions and seemed to agree, albeit reluctantly, with the idea of arresting Palpatine and stripping him of his office. When news of Kenobi's victory reached Coruscant, Windu felt ready to demand that Supreme Chancellor Palpatine relinquish his emergency powers at last. As Windu prepared for a meeting with the [[Chair of the Senate/Legends|Senate Chair]] to bring him news of the elimination of General Grievous, a distraught Anakin Skywalker arrived and confirmed the Jedi Council's greatest fear: the elected leader of the Galactic Republic was in fact the Sith Lord Darth Sidious. Master Windu ordered Skywalker to wait in the Jedi Council Chamber for his return and boarded a gunship along with the nervous Nautolan Jedi Master Kit Fisto, the [[Iktotchi/Legends|Iktotchi]] Jedi Master Saesee Tiin and the Zabrak Jedi Master [[Agen Kolar/Legends|Agen Kolar]]. Tiin And Windu tended to their teammates concerns as they departed to [[Showdown on Coruscant|confront]] the Chancellor. ===Final battle and death=== {{Quote|I'm going to end this once and for all!|Mace Windu|}} [[File:DuelonCoruscant.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Jedi confront Darth Sidious.]] The Jedi marched into Palpatine's office and Windu promptly announced that the Chancellor was under arrest to face trial before the Senate. Due to Palpatine's defiance (declaring himself as ''the'' Senate), he finally revealed his true colors. Darth Sidious ignited his crimson lightsaber and with a [[Force scream/Legends|battle cry]], flew through the air and [[Shiak|stabbed]] Kolar. Before he could strike Sidious from behind, Tiin was also struck down. Masters Windu and Fisto managed to defend against the initial assaults, but even Fisto's mastery of [[Form I/Legends|Shii-Cho]] was overwhelmed by the intensity of Sidious's swordplay. Fisto was slashed across the waist and died with his signature smile, leaving Master Windu to fight Sidious alone. His mastery of [[Form VII/Legends|Vaapad]] served him well in countering Sidious's Dark Side mastery. [[File:Coruscant_Duel.png|left|thumb|251x251px|Windu and Sidious battle.]] The two viciously battled through the Chancellor's private office and lounging room into his main office. Noticing the immeasurable connection his opponent held with the Dark Side, Windu surrendered himself completley to the essentials of Vaapad: to enjoy the thrill of battle, to fight on instinct. Fully unleashing the power of his lightsaber style, Windu forced all of Sidious's dark energy back at him in an equally chaotic, quick series of attacks. Driving Sidious back with an offensive march, Windu steered the battle towards the office bay-window, which was promptly shattered by their whirling blades. By bringing the duel to the ledge of the window-sill above the sheer drop of the Coruscant cityscape, Windu prompted Sidious to channel more energy into a Force-powered grip on the ledge, and less into the Force powered speed that he was using against Windu. Suddenly, he felt Anakin Skywalker approaching the office and an overwhelming sense of fear. This was the tipping point, for Windu deduced that Skywalker was Sidious' shatterpoint. As the Jedi realized the depth of the Sith Lord's trust in Skywalker, Sidious tried to knock Windu over the ledge. Recovering in time,[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]] Windu delivered a well-placed kick to Sidious' face, which caused him to drop his saber into the streets below. Skywalker appeared just as Windu cornered Sidious and again stated that he was under arrest. When the Jedi Master proclaimed Sidious defeated, this enraged the Sith Lord. He unleashed a barrage of [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]] against Windu, driving him back. Grunting with exertion, Windu redirected the lightning back with his lightsaber, melting away the Chancellor's features in a display of the "superconducting loop" of Vaapad. Horrified, Skywalker watched the Jedi Master brutally contend with Sidious. As they struggled, they each implored Skywalker to help them, each trying to convince him of the other's treachery. Eventually Sidious ceased his barrage, claiming he could no longer maintain his attack against Windu, exclaiming that he had become too weak. Skywalker believed that if Sidious died, any chance of saving Padmé from certain death would be lost. Skywalker told Windu that the Sith Lord should stand trial and that killing him was not the Jedi way, but Windu determined that the man, both as Palpatine and Sidious, was too dangerous to be kept alive because he had control of the Galactic Senate and the Courts. Sidious pleaded for Skywalker's help, as Windu moved to strike the Dark Lord. [[File:MaceWinduDeath-ROTS.png|thumb|250px|Master Windu blasted by Sidious's lightning.]] With Windu's attention focused entirely on Sidious, he failed to foresee Skywalker's intervention. Skywalker ignited his own lightsaber and [[Cho mai/Legends|severed the Jedi Master's lightsaber hand]], as he looked down with his lightsaber falling off the edge of the building, leaving him defenseless against the full power of Sidious's Force lightning. Shocked, Windu realized he had been too focused on Sidious and consequently had failed to sense Skywalker's own shatterpoint. As the Chancellor ranted, he once again unleashed his rage, blasting raw dark side energy through Windu's body, sending him hurtling out the window into the cityscape, where he would certainly have been killed upon hitting the surface miles below. At fifty-three years of age and after decades of serving the Jedi Council, Master Windu was dead.''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' With a single stroke, Sidious had removed one of the few Jedi who posed any threat to him and secured the allegiance of the promising Anakin Skywalker. With Windu's death, Skywalker was transformed into Darth Vader and the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]] had begun. ===Legacy=== Windu was [[Anti-Jedi sentiment/Legends|scapegoated]] by the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]] as the primary villain behind the alleged "Jedi Rebellion". Less than a week after his death, various media outlets began circulating ''[[The Private Journals of Mace Windu]]'', an alleged first-person account of Windu's many years of scheming to conquer the Republic. In truth the journals were fabrications and Imperial propaganda, in which various portions of Windu's actual journal from the Clone Wars had been included to give them credibility. In 18 BBY, a [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] sold a broken lightsaber to Senator [[Sano Sauro]] claiming it once belonged to Windu. The Duros said he had found it on a street in the lower levels of Coruscant. Sano would later display the lightsaber in his office.''[[The Last of the Jedi: Return of the Dark Side]]'' Mace Windu's killer, Darth Sidious, referred to him as a mighty Jedi rumored to have possessed the only purple lightsaber for a great span of time. This was in order to convince Mara Jade that she was special and cared for when he conferred upon her a purple blade.[[Allegiance (novel)|''Allegiance'']] During the Galactic Civil War, bootleg HoloNet broadcasts were made showing animations of Windu's activities during the Battle of Dantooine. The Imperial Security Bureau unsuccessfully attempted to stamp them out, as they were a large recruiting tool for the Alliance to Restore the Republic. Years after the fall of Palpatine's [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the creation of [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker's]] [[New Jedi Order]], Windu's reputation had officially been restored to its former glory and he was remembered as a hero of the Clone Wars. Several Jedi, most notably [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]]—Anakin Skywalker's granddaughter—were known to refer to him as "a great Jedi Master" and revered his abilities, most notably that of the shatterpoint.''[[Legacy of the Force: Invincible]]'' ==Personality and traits== {{Expandsect}} {{Quote|You see things with ''hope'' in your eyes. You believe that, given a true choice, people will choose the light. That is your ''flaw'' and your ''strength''."
"Hope must be tempered by ''reality''.|T'ra Saa and Mace Windu|[[Republic 66|''Republic'' 66]]}} [[File:Windu_Angry.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Mace Windu, Jedi Master.]] Mace Windu was a unique personality among the Jedi: he was serious, noted for his grim demeanor and very cautious, to the point of occasional reluctance, a careful chooser of his friends, and being slow to trust. Despite this, he was extremely courageous, bravely risking life and limb on numerous occasions for the Galactic Republic and its people. He also has a certain value for life, opposing the constant attempts to kill the mighty Zillo Beast, which he correctly presumed to be the last of its species. He was intelligent, wise and perceptive, strongly believing in the Jedi's role as the servants of the Republic's underlying principles rather than its masters, and treated all civilians with respect. Windu also was willing to go to great lengths to ensure the well being of the innocent. Likewise, he would use his Force powers to save the soldiers under his command from death. He was also willing to take the time to bury fallen soldiers, honoring their sacrifice. A wise Jedi Master, Windu emphasized the importance of keeping an open mind and heart and cared for his fellow Jedi deeply. He developed a strong bond with his padawan, Depa Billaba, even seen her as a daughter, yet, staying true to the teaching of the Jedi Code, was able to love her without being attached, and stopping her when Billaba lost to the dark side of the Force. Windu was a man of few words and maintained a stoic attitude. He was highly confident in his abilities, sometimes to point of pridefulness, and was known to be outspoken, stubborn, and occasionally sarcastic. Windu was also prone to being suspicious and mistrustful of others, particularly politicians who he held in low regard, and leading him to become cold and harsh to those Jedi he thought had betrayed him and the Jedi Council. During the Clone Wars, Windu questioned the Jedi’s role. He grew concerned about their place in a Republic growing increasingly corrupt, and the contradiction of leading armies and sending soldiers to their deaths—actions opposed to their traditional role as peacekeepers .Yet at the same time, Windu believed the Jedi had always taken the lead in times of conflict, doing what was necessary when peace failed. To him, the war, however tragic, was a duty the Order could not ignore. Ultimately, Windu's motivation, beyond his light side and Jedi beliefs, was a belief that peace was created by civilization. Viewing the Republic as the ultimate civilization, he developed an attachment towards it and a willingness to do whatever was required to preserve it. This attachment would cost him his life in battle against Darth Sidious when his readiness to kill the Sith Lord in cold blood drove a desperate Anakin Skywalker to act against him. ==Powers and abilities== {{Quote|Vaapad is as aggressive and powerful as its namesake, but its power comes at great risk: immersion in Vaapad opens the gates that restrain one's inner darkness. To use Vaapad, a Jedi must allow himself to enjoy the fight; he must give himself over to the thrill of battle. The rush of winning. Vaapad is a path that leads through the penumbra of the dark side…This was Vaapad's ultimate test.|Mace Windu on Vaapad|}} ===Lightsaber training=== [[File:Mace_Unleashed.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Windu utilizing Vaapad.]] Having chosen the path of the Jedi Guardian, Mace Windu's training was mostly focused on mastering lightsaber combat, becoming an incredibly formidable and skilled warrior and was eventually considered to be one of the greatest swordsmen ever produced by the Jedi Order. One of the greatest duelists in history and among the greatest in his time, he was considered to be second only to the venerable Grand Master Yoda in skill among the Jedi. Although Dooku had once bested him in a friendly duel,''[[Power of the Jedi Sourcebook]]'' during the Clone Wars, Windu was considered to be the only one who could stand toe-to-toe with his former friend in neutral ground, despite Dooku, now Darth Tyranus, having improved his abilities further from his training with Sidious. Indeed, he had proved to be able to duel Tyranus evenly, forcing the Sith Lord to resort to calling upon his MagnaGuards to hold off Windu. Alongside Obi-Wan Kenobi, Windu managed to defeat Tyranus on Behpour. Another display of Windu's outstanding prowess in lightsaber combat was how he could overwhelm General Griveous in single combat, a cyborg who had killed dozens of highly capable Jedi and quickly overpower Asajj Ventress in their first duel, though at the time he was going all out.{{FactFile|108|MAC 13-16|Mace Windu}} He had held his own against an improved Ventress in their second encounter, even if they had been forced to end it prematurely by circumstantial factors.{{TCWComicCite|6.23|Fashion}} Though he stated that Depa Billaba's bladework potentially surpassed his, and while she was even more formidable than she usually was due to tapping into the deaths of many of Kar Vastor's guards, Windu was still able to hold off her and eventually lure her into destroying the spaceport's signal jammer in their ferociously intense duel. However, he clearly had to put in great effort in fighting her and was close to being defeated; both combatants were severely hampered by physical weakness, so the fight would have been close. Windu also managed to duel equally with Sora Bulq, despite his claims of having improved from having perfected Vaapad with the dark side. Windu even managed to draw power from the current Dark Lord of the Sith to disarm Darth Sidious himself—a feat only replicated by the Grand Masters Yoda and (boosted by the power of his family) Luke Skywalker.{{Film|III}}[[Dark Empire 6|''Dark Empire'' 6]] He acknowledged that they would have fought to a draw if Windu had not used shatterpoint; furthermore, he never fully realized that he was drawing upon Anakin Skywalker's fear at the time. Known for having fully mastered all the seven combat forms and every stance and technique of lightsaber combat, alongside Sora Bulq, Windu developed the deadly form of [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|combat]] known as Vaapad, the seventh form of combat which completed (to the Jedi) the Juyo form. Vaapad was named after a [[Vaapad/Legends|predator]] native to the moons of [[Sarapin/Legends|Sarapin]], which was intentionally created to allow him and those he trusted with the form to channel the darkness within and also that of the enemy to use against them. [[File:MaceWindu_CN.png|thumb|left|200px|Mace Windu during the Clone Wars.]] Master Windu was the only Jedi to ''fully'' master Vaapad, though Quinlan Vos could count as a close second. The other two practitioners of the style, Sora Bulq and Depa Billaba, were unable to master it—instead, it mastered them, driving them insane and leading them to the dark side. When Windu went to Haruun Kal in search for Depa, he displayed masterful skill in [[Jar'Kai/Legends|Jar'Kai]], effectively adapting Vaapad into dual-blade combat. Although Windu primarily used Vaapad, he at times also applied his mastery of the other forms to supplement his use of the form he created with aspects from other forms. In addition to using a Form V opening stance in the middle of his battle with Darth Sidious, Windu was highly proficient in deflection, which likely showed outstanding skill in either [[Form III/Legends|Form III/Soresu]] or [[Form V/Legends|Form V/Shien]], as shown by how he was one of the few Jedi to survive the Battle of Geonosis, deflecting any shot sent at him by the overwhelmingly massive droid forces in order to survive long enough for Yoda and the clones to aid. He also displayed proficiency in applying Force attacks in his lightsaber sequence, apparently showing his superb mastery of [[Form VI/Legends|Form VI/Niman]]. He also often employed a behind the back parry and then thrust sequence in his dueling style. ===Force Mastery=== [[File:Macehands.jpg|thumb|Windu destroying droids on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]] with his bare hands.]] Known to be one of the greatest Force users in the Jedi, Mace Windu's mastery and power in the Force was incredible. He was known for his resistance to the lures of the dark side, channeling his inner darkness into his attacks to help him serve the light side of the Force. This allowed him to utilize some of the darkest powers known to either Jedi or Sith without succumbing to his aggression, such as the terrible Force Crush. His mastery of the form he created, Vaapad, also proved his devotion to the light, as the only two other advanced users, Depa Billaba and Sora Bulq, fell to the dark side. Master Windu was known to be able to ponder matters of the dark and light sides of the Force with a clarity perhaps second only to Master Yoda. Windu was known to be highly proficient in using the Force to enhance the capabilities of his body, and as such, was able to [[Force jump/Legends|leap]] to great heights and across enormous distances. On Haruun Kal, he went toe-to-toe with Kar Vastor, and demonstrated incredible [[Force speed/Legends|Force enhanced speed]] by landing six blows to the man's body before he could blink; however, for all his speed, he could not come to the aid of his fellow Jedi Masters in time when Darth Sidious made the first move. On Dantooine, having lost his lightsaber, Windu took to tearing super battle droids apart with his bare hands, showing incredible [[Enhance Attribute|Force strength]] and resilience as he crushed armor and tore out circuitry with his fingers. Another incredible feat of the body Windu demonstrated during the Battle of Dantooine was "riding" a landslide of rock and earth weighing hundreds of tons. Machines were his to [[Technometry|manipulate]] with the Force.''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]'' The Korun Jedi Master's skill with telekinesis was so extensive that during the Battle of Ryloth, he was capable of Force pushing a huge AT-TE walker off of a cliff with apparent ease. He also demonstrated the ability to simultaneously levitate two clone troopers with the Force and move them swiftly across the length of a bridge. He also ripped down a gigantic door, in order to destroy a Separatist tank and associated infantry support. In addition, Windu proved able to release a torrent of Force energy capable of blasting several droids backwards and powerful enough to destroy them on impact with the ground. The range of his Force thrown objects such as a B2 Battle Droid could reach almost three kilometers.{{CWACite|1|Heavy Metal Jedi}} He even telekinetically removed the bolts of a super battle droid during the Battle of Dantooiee, allowing the droid to fall to pieces. He was incredibly proficient in the application of the [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Wave|Force Wave]] power, and used it to an incredible degree during the battles of Dantooine and Coruscant; blasting away and instantly destroying dozens of droids away from him with a single kinetic blast. He was among a group of Jedi who used [[Force bellow]], though Darth Sidious was unable to tell if he personally used this power to hurl away the Redrobes and break open the door to Palpatine's office. The Jedi Master also demonstrated an affinity for using darker telekinetic powers, such as [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Grip|Force Grip]] and [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Crush|Force Crush]], the latter of which he used to severely injure the fearsome General Grievous. [[File:Shatterpoint.png|thumb|left|250px|Mace Windu using the "Shatterpoint".]] Aiding Windu throughout his life was also his [[Shatterpoint/Legends|shatterpoint]] ability, a power he always had a natural affinity for. It allowed him to see weak points in opponents, events, and everyday life. This power also allowed a Jedi to shatter otherwise unbreakable objects by channeling the Force into the places of the object that bound it together. Windu's shatterpoint ability proved vital to his victory over Darth Sidious, but he had realized too late that the shatterpoint was Anakin Skywalker's, not Sidious'. ===Other abilities=== Despite the darker aspects of his nature and his incredible fighting prowess, Mace Windu was also extremely well-known for his diplomacy, with his use of words and legendary reputation settling many conflicts without incident. His skills as a diplomat, along with his courage, integrity, and skill, garnered him the position as a highly-respected Senior Jedi High Council member. Master Windu was also an adept pilot as displayed during the battle of Coruscant. He was, however, shot down during the battle.''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]'' ==Behind the scenes== ===Character concept=== [[File:UnknownDarkSiderAdept.jpg|thumb|200px|Concept art of Mace Windu.]] The name "[[Mace Windy]]" actually dates back to the earliest incarnation of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'']], a two-page outline written by George Lucas in [[1973]] called ''[[Journal of the Whills, Part I]]''. The character [[Windy Starkiller|Windy Marstrap]] is also derived from early incarnations of Mace Windu, becoming variously a brother of [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia]] in the rough draft and a friend of Luke's in the third draft.''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]'' A similar name—[[Mace Towani]]—appeared in the made-for-television Ewok films ''[[Caravan of Courage: An Ewok Adventure]]'' ([[1984]]) and ''[[Ewoks: The Battle for Endor]]'' ([[1985]]). An alien in [[Spare Parts (short story)|''Spare Parts'']] (c. [[1994]]) and ''[[Galaxy Guide 7: Mos Eisley]]'' ([[1993]]) also went by the name of Mace Windu, an abbreviation of his full name [[Macemillian-winduarté]]. The name Mace Windu was finally introduced into the films with [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']] ([[1999]]). Although a [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] article mentioning Mace Windu's participation in the [[Battle of Skor II]] explains Macemillian-winduarté's name, the coexistence of the names "Mace Towani" and "Mace Windu" may imply that "Mace" was a common name throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], or that Towani was simply named after Windu due to Windu's fame (given the fact that the Ewok films take place during the Galactic Civil War). Early Star Wars Comics and Action Figures (usually ones released around the time of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I]]) depict Mace Windu with a blue blade rather than his traditional purple blade. This is presumably made canon by adding the story of Windu having made a blue lightsaber and alternating the use of the purple one with that one.
